summary:
EarthBeat is an interactive climate sonification experience developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: The Earth Information Jukebox. It transforms NASA's monthly global temperature anomaly data from the GISTEMP v4 dataset into sound, allowing users to explore the changing climate record through both visualization and listening.

By mapping real temperature anomaly values to musical tones using browser-based audio synthesis, EarthBeat creates an alternative way to experience long-term climate patterns. Users can explore the data timeline, view the corresponding chart, and hear how the signal changes over time. The project connects NASA's Climate Spiral visualization with data-driven sonification to make climate information more engaging, accessible, and memorable.

EarthBeat demonstrates how scientific data can become an interactive sensory experience without losing its connection to the underlying measurements.
details:
What EarthBeat does

EarthBeat explores climate change through data-driven sonification. It connects NASA's Earth Information Center visualization context with monthly global temperature anomaly observations from NASA's GISTEMP v4 dataset.

The application processes the monthly data and maps temperature anomaly values to sound parameters. Using the Web Audio API, it generates tones directly in the browser, allowing users to listen to how the climate signal changes across the available historical timeline.

How it works

  1. Data source: Monthly global Land-Ocean Temperature Index (LOTI) anomalies are obtained from NASA GISTEMP v4.
  2. Data processing: The application parses the observations, handles missing values, and uses the historical period corresponding to the NASA Climate Spiral visualization (1880–2022).
  3. Sonification: A deterministic mapping translates the temperature anomaly values into audio parameters.
  4. Interactive exploration: Users can play, pause, and navigate the timeline while viewing the corresponding data and mapped frequency readout.

Technology

  • React and TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Web Audio API for browser-based sound synthesis
  • NASA GISTEMP v4 scientific dataset
  • NASA Scientific Visualization Studio Climate Spiral
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript

Innovation and impact

EarthBeat offers an alternative way to engage with climate information by combining visual exploration with sound. It aims to make long-term scientific patterns more intuitive and memorable, particularly for people who may find conventional charts and numerical datasets difficult to interpret.

The sonification is an artistic representation of measured scientific values, not a recording of sounds produced by Earth. The application retains the original data context, units, baseline information, and source attribution to encourage responsible interpretation.

EarthBeat is an independent educational project created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 and is not an official NASA product.
